title: Multi-Agentic Approach for History Matching of Oil Reservoirs
authors: Linar Samigullin; Sergei Shumilin; Evgeny Burnaev
task: automate configuration and execution of reservoir history-matching workflows (parameter selection, optimizer choice, simulator execution, diagnostic reporting) via natural language
tools_used: ECLIPSE .DATA file exploration and modification tools; validation tools for modified ECLIPSE input decks; RAG over OPM simulator documentation/manual; OPM Flow simulation backend; Bayesian optimization with Gaussian Process surrogate models
evaluation_method: evaluated on three reservoir models of increasing complexity (SPE1 synthetic, SPE9 faulted benchmark, Norne real-field model) using weighted normalized root mean square error (wNRMSE) as the objective
reported_result: reduces the mismatch by 95% on SPE1, 69% on SPE9, and 13% on Norne (wNRMSE from 2.312 to 2.013 on Norne)
maturity_claimed: This design enables users to initiate and steer history matching through natural language while preserving explicit control over selected parameters and optimization settings.
author_stated_limitations: Future work should focus on enhancing the RAG system to cover more nuanced simulator behaviour, implementing long-term memory for iterative multi-stage history matching, and refining the agent graph architecture to accommodate alternative workflows and multi-cycle campaigns.

title: AI Agent for Reverse-Engineering Legacy Finite-Difference Code and Translating to Devito
authors: Yinghan Hou; Zongyou Yang
task: reverse-engineer legacy Fortran finite-difference code and translate it into the Devito domain-specific language used for seismic wave-equation modelling
tools_used: Neo4j-based knowledge graph store; Fortran static analysis (FortranCodeAnalyzer); BGE-M3 embedding model for semantic similarity; Ruff code formatter; Pydantic structured-output constraints; LangGraph workflow orchestration
evaluation_method: eleven benchmark queries across three complexity tiers plus 13 constructed Devito finite-difference test cases; retrieval scored by Precision@5/Recall@5/MRR; code translation scored by G-Eval combined with static analysis (execution correctness, structural soundness, mathematical consistency, API compliance)
reported_result: Precision@5 of 0.964 and Recall@5 of 0.930 (MRR 1.000); Grade-A success rate of 76.9% across 13 test cases; 5.75x throughput improvement with four concurrent agents (22.8 to 131.2 files per hour)
maturity_claimed: not stated
author_stated_limitations: the system's capabilities for advanced data mining and pattern discovery remain limited; the existing quality evaluation framework relies on fixed, predefined thresholds, such as excellent_threshold=0.85 and acceptable_threshold=0.55...the system's adaptability across diverse conversion scenarios is constrained by this static configuration

title: TREMORS: An Agentic Assistant for Multi-Datacenter Seismic Data Acquisition
authors: Ryley G. Hill; Richard Alfaro-Diaz; Jonathan MacCarthy; Jonas A. Kintner; Christopher W. Johnson
task: translate natural-language scientific intent into structured, reproducible seismic data-retrieval workflows across multiple datacenters
tools_used: FDSN webservices via the ObsPy API, interfacing with datacenters including EARTHSCOPE, ORFEUS, GEOFON, SCEDC, NCEDC
evaluation_method: two illustrative example workflows (event-based and continuous waveform acquisition) demonstrating natural-language-to-schema translation and execution; no formal benchmark or quantitative comparison reported
reported_result: not stated
maturity_claimed: While agents are not yet capable of replacing high-level subject matter experts or independently producing scientific discovery, TREMORS represents an important first step in assisting scientists with routine data retrieval tasks.
author_stated_limitations: The semantic parsing stage may fail for ambiguous, imprecise, or unusually phrased prompts.; TREMORS depends on external FDSN services and ObsPy-compatible interfaces, making it sensitive to heterogeneous metadata standards, incomplete station information, service outages, and variability across datacenters.

title: An LLM-agent interface for end-to-end probabilistic seismic hazard and risk analysis
authors: Sreenath Vemula; Pierre Jehel; Fabrice Cotton; Filippo Gatti
task: agentic interface to the end-to-end probabilistic seismic hazard and risk chain
base_model: Claude Sonnet 4.6; local 7B model (tool-selection accuracy test)
tools_used: OpenQuake engine and the 2020 European Seismic Hazard and Risk Model (ESHM20) via 24 typed MCP endpoints: hazard curves, uniform hazard spectra, conditional mean spectra, fragility assessment, loss estimation
evaluation_method: benchmarked against ESHM20 published values at 73 cities; governing equations verified against external references; tool-selection accuracy tested with a local 7B model and Claude Sonnet 4.6
reported_result: median absolute ln-residual of 0.05 at the 475-year return period (about 5%; mean 0.07)
maturity_claimed: A full hazard-to-loss estimate runs in minutes.
author_stated_limitations: Hazard is evaluated deterministically on the highest-weighted source and ground-motion branches, rather than by Monte-Carlo sampling of the full logic tree; the default branch subsets evaluate the dominant axes of the ESHM20 logic tree, but not every authorized branch.

title: GeoMind: An Agentic Workflow for Lithology Classification with Reasoned Tool Invocation
authors: Mingyue Cheng; Yitong Zhou; Jiahao Wang; Qingyang Mao; Qi Liu
task: tool-augmented agentic framework for lithology classification from well logs via reasoned tool invocation
base_model: Qwen3-4B (fine-tuned); GPT-5 used as offline teacher model
tools_used: Case Retriever; Trend Pattern Extractor; Neighbor Vote Aggregator; Neural Probability Interpreter; Semantic Reasoning Engine; Consensus Conflict Scanner; Stratigraphic Sequence Validator
evaluation_method: evaluated on four public well-log benchmark datasets (SEAM, Facies, FORCE, GeoLink) using weighted-average Precision, Recall and F1, compared against 17 baseline methods
baseline: nn-DTW, GBDT, XGBoost, LSTMFCN, MLP, InceptionTime, MiniRocket, MOMENT, BiGRU-CRF, Inception-Geol, GIAT, InstructTime, GPT4TS, TableTime
maturity_claimed: GeoMind consistently achieves superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods
author_stated_limitations: trained and evaluated on a machine equipped with 4x NVIDIA A800 GPUs, due to the additional memory and compute overhead introduced by multi-stage tool invocation

title: TADI: Tool-Augmented Drilling Intelligence via Agentic LLM Orchestration over Heterogeneous Wellsite Data
authors: Rong Lu
task: agentic AI system that transforms drilling operational data into evidence-based analytical intelligence
tools_used: twelve domain-specialized tools (query_drilling_data, search_daily_reports, get_well_overview, get_drilling_phases, compute_efficiency_metrics, compare_wells, get_bha_configurations, identify_operational_issues, get_field_benchmarks, get_formation_context, generate_depth_time_plot, get_ddr_narrative) over a DuckDB structured store and a ChromaDB semantic store
evaluation_method: 95 automated tests plus a 130-question stress-question taxonomy across six operational categories; three case studies; qualitative ablation analysis; compared against Direct-LLM and Simple-RAG baselines (qualitative expectation baselines, not executed benchmark results)
baseline: Direct LLM (no tools); Simple RAG (retrieve + generate)
reported_result: parses all 1,759 DDR XML files with zero errors; DuckDB over 12 tables with 65,447 rows; ChromaDB over 36,709 embedded documents
maturity_claimed: The complete 6,084-line, framework-free implementation is reproducible given the public Volve download and an API key.
author_stated_limitations: sparse-data wells produce lower-quality answers due to insufficient data for reliable phase detection; evaluation used qualitative expectation baselines rather than executed benchmark results; future work includes quantitative evaluation of all 130 stress test questions with human expert scoring to validate the EGS metric

title: Advancing Subsurface Discovery and Geothermal Monitoring with an Agentic Artificial Intelligence Framework

evaluation_method: RAGAS-framework benchmark test set of curated geothermal-related scenarios (response accuracy, relevancy, faithfulness) plus a physics-aware inversion experiment combining GAIA with AlphaEvolve
baseline: baseline Gemma 4 without RAG; AlphaEvolve baseline

author_stated_limitations: "we plan to explore domain-focused LLMs that are fine-tuned on geothermal-specific data."; "we plan to incorporate surrogate modeling techniques into GAIA DT."; "we plan to explore the use of self-evolving multi-agent systems in GAIA."

title: AGENTS4GEOS: agentic platform for open-source multi-physics simulation
authors: Adriano Cortês; Roberto M. Velho; Fernando A. Rochinha; Álvaro L. G. A. Coutinho; Mauricio Araya-Polo; Hervé Gross

title: Sim2Schedule: A Simulator-Guided LLM Framework for Autonomous Open-Pit Mine Scheduling
authors: Mustavi Ibne Masum; Thiago Eustaquio Alves de Oliveira; Mahzabeen Emu
task: autonomous open-pit mine extraction/processing scheduling under geotechnical and capacity constraints
tools_used: custom mining simulator enforcing geotechnical precedence/capacity/extraction-processing coupling in its action-generation mechanism; Ollama local LLM deployment; Gurobi MILP solver used to build the benchmark (not an agent-callable tool)
evaluation_method: evaluated across mining instances of 18-45 blocks against a novel MILP formulation, a greedy heuristic, and random selection, measuring NPV recovery, optimality gap, and execution time
baseline: MILP optimal solution; greedy heuristic; random selection
reported_result: LLM framework "recovers between 94% and 99% of the MILP optimal NPV while scaling linearly in computation time"
maturity_claimed: achieving "real-time adaptability and zero-shot generalization"
author_stated_limitations: Future work will extend evaluation to larger real-world block models; the study incorporates no geological grade uncertainty and commodity price variability; DeepSeek demonstrates reduced robustness at larger scales; the framework yields near-optimal rather than guaranteed-optimal solutions

title: SeisEvo: Evolution of Seismic Data Reconstruction Algorithms by Agents
authors: Yingjie Xu; Siwei Yu; Jianwei Ma
task: LLM-driven multi-agent search that evolves an explicit, inspectable seismic-reconstruction algorithm rather than a single reconstruction result
tools_used: EvE (Evolutionary Ensemble of Agents), a decentralized evolutionary framework of multiple coding agents that iteratively propose and refine candidate programs; execution-based scoring; hard physical-constraint gate rejecting invalid candidates
evaluation_method: SNR comparison against classical algorithms across missing ratios from 30% to 70%, with candidates scored on search-time sub-blocks and external data accessed only after the operator was fixed, then tested on data not used during search
baseline: classic POCS; classic MSSA; "a stronger rank-reduction baseline"
reported_result: "Evo-POCS improves the SNR over classic POCS by 3.49 dB on average across missing ratios from 30% to 70%"; "Evo-MSSA improves the average reconstruction SNR by more than 7 dB over classic MSSA and by more than 3 dB over a stronger rank-reduction baseline"
maturity_claimed: "this is the first study to formulate the design of a seismic reconstruction operator as a constrained, LLM-driven program evolution task"
author_stated_limitations: The main cost at present is offline search computation, substantially more expensive than running a fixed hand-designed solver; a single trajectory per case is not sufficient to decide whether the search budget is adequate; the present evidence is restricted to seismic data reconstruction, extension to other tasks remains a hypothesis to be tested rather than a demonstrated capability; gains decrease as the missing ratio becomes more severe

maturity_claimed: LandslideAgent further enables autonomous multi-source spatial data inference, realizing full-process intelligence for landslide identification and analysis
author_stated_limitations: Pervasive spectral confusion driven by high intra-class variance and inter-class similarity imposes a persistent bottleneck on fine-grained classification; future work will transition LandslideAgent from a static scene interpreter to a dynamic, continuous-monitoring intelligent system

title: LLM-assisted workflow for geological unit harmonization and tectonic-unit-constrained map generalization with copper occurrence overlay
authors: Muhammad Atif Bilal; Yongzhi Wang; Kateryna Hlyniana; Fahad Hameed; Muhammad Saleem Mughal
task: harmonize heterogeneous geological unit descriptions into age-based labels, then generalize maps under tectonic-unit constraints with a copper occurrence overlay
agentic_techniques: not stated ("the language model is used only to harmonize heterogeneous geological unit descriptions into a controlled set of age-based labels"; the remaining steps are "a deterministic GIS workflow")
tools_used: a deterministic GIS workflow performing "tectonic-unit-constrained partitioning, polygon merging, topology cleaning, and regional clipping"; "point-in-polygon overlay"; a coordinate-based (K = 3) Gaussian Mixture Model "selected through AIC, BIC, component-size, and assignment-stability diagnostics"
evaluation_method: "In the Chagai Belt study window", measuring polygon-part, vertex-count and boundary-length reduction and the copper assignment rate
reported_result: "the workflow reduced polygon parts by 19.9%, vertex count by 9.9%, and boundary length by 10.0%, while maintaining a copper assignment rate of 96.4%"
maturity_claimed: "These results demonstrate a reproducible approach for geological unit harmonization and tectonic-unit-constrained map generalization"
author_stated_limitations: "Maximum posterior membership probability is used only to quantify separation among the fitted spatial components and does not represent geological confidence or mineral prospectivity"

title: Large language model-based multi-agent systems for automated foundation design: router-driven task classification and expert selection framework
authors: Sompote Youwai; David Phim; Vianne Gayl Murcia; Rianne Clair Onas
task: automated foundation design calculations through router-driven task classification and expert agent selection
agentic_techniques: role-specialisation;guardrails-validation;human-in-the-loop; router-based expert selection and a designer-checker configuration
base_model: DeepSeek R1, ChatGPT 4 Turbo, Grok 3 and Gemini 2.5 Pro (compared as baseline models)
tools_used: shallow foundation and pile design calculations; "The dual-tier classification framework" distinguishing foundation types
evaluation_method: "Initial evaluation on 27 test cases with triple-trial execution", comparing three configurations: "single-agent processing, multi-agent designer-checker architecture, and router-based expert selection"

author_stated_limitations: "the limited sample size necessitates comprehensive validation on larger, more diverse datasets before deployment recommendations"; "Safety–critical requirements necessitate continued human oversight in professional applications"

title: MAS-LAND: A Multi-Agent System for Landslide detection and rapid response
authors: Abdelkader Riche; Abdallah Zeggada; Francesco Caleca; Mohammed Alruqimi; Pierluigi Confuorto; Mawloud Guermoui; Silvia Bianchini; Veronica Tofani; Farid Melgani
task: post-event landslide detection, infrastructure exposure assessment and automated reporting for civil protection operations
agentic_techniques: role-specialisation;tool-calling;guardrails-validation; a reporting agent "operated in deterministic mode" and "a transparent, rule-based decision matrix"

maturity_claimed: "the delivery of a fully integrated, post-event pipeline"; "the results demonstrate the potential of multi-agent, hybrid AI–geospatial architectures to enhance situational awareness"
author_stated_limitations: not stated ("pronounced class imbalance" is described as a condition performance held up under, not as a limitation of the framework)
